Kel

Overview

Kel is a thief from Suslanger and Kir’s travelling companion in Lost in Astral. She saves his life in the slave pen, helps him escape and accompanies him through Gipath and Ingos to Jigran. Her contacts, quick thinking and willingness to challenge him make her an active partner in his search. She falls in love with him, although he is slow to recognise it. Kel can be resurrected after her scripted death: the optional Rod of Life route returns her to the party. The guide below explains the three fragments and the conversation that decides her fate. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]

Character and loyalties

Kel hides concern behind jokes, taunts and a habit of speaking about herself in the third person. She spots expensive tricks and wounded pride quickly: Kir’s costly disguise amuses her, Feiruz’s vanity gives her a way to recruit him, and Stark’s reluctance to learn becomes obvious to her. Her loyalty also has limits and demands of its own. After Feiruz’s death she insists on vengeance under the thieves’ code, despite Kir’s objections. When Dartas insults her, she rejects pity and makes her anger clear. Her affection for Kir does not erase her judgement or her ties to other people. [8, 2, 9, 10, 11]

Kel and the slave pen

Soldiers beat Kir nearly to death. In the slave pen, Kel nurses him back to consciousness, shortens his name to Kir and offers a partnership in escape. He initially hopes to explain the mistake to the authorities; the official instead assigns work according to the prisoners’ abilities. Kel has overheard that an officer possesses a map of the catacombs. Their escape coincides with the Horror’s attack on the slave camp: guards die and the camp burns. They obtain the map and take the catacombs out of the fortress area. Kel, usually so confident, admits her unease about the dark underground route. Once outside, Kel proposes refuge with an acquaintance who collects spiders. Their relationship begins in this shared dependence: Kir needs her local knowledge, and Kel needs a partner. [1, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20]

Suslanger: contacts and confidence

After the escape, Kel directs Kir to Rindeil’s house. She knows enough of his habits to warn Kir that promises of help come second to his spiders. When she sees Kir’s new face wrapping, she points out how much money he has spent on looking poor and rejoins him to keep other rogues from exploiting him. Later, the locked meteorite chest requires Feiruz’s skill. Kel turns his refusal into a challenge to his nerve and reputation as a thief. His agreement creates a debt that draws them into the rescue of Alia. [17, 8, 21, 22, 23, 2, 24, 25]

Feiruz and the thieves’ code

Feiruz dies during Aliya’s rescue. Kel has seen who struck the fatal blow and tells the grieving Aliya to rally their comrades. Kir objects to another killing, but Kel insists that the thieves must avenge one of their own. The episode shows a harder side of the woman who saved him: she can be tender toward Kir and uncompromising about obligations he does not share. [25, 9, 26]

Staying with Kir

Their journey takes them from Suslanger through Gipath and Ingos. When the hidden road to Jigran finally appears, Kel admits that the unknown destination frightens her. Kir decides to go immediately, believing that he now has the strength to face Firez himself. She corrects his assumption that he will travel alone: they are going together. Kir had expected her to remain with Trickster, but she tells him she prefers him. Her decision brings her into a war for a homeland that is his, not hers. [27, 3, 28]

Dartas, Kel and the duel

Dartas treats Kel as someone he is entitled to possess, insults her attachment to Kir and refuses to accept rejection. When Kir confronts him, Dartas asks what he wants in exchange for her and then calls him a coward. They duel on Death Island. Defeated and spared, Dartas admits despair over Dar-Ulgorn’s loss and his family’s future. Kir answers with his own enslavement, escape and determination to fight, winning Dartas’s respect. Kel initially believes the duel means that Kir has recognised her feelings; he disappoints her by calling it a defence of his own honour. The baron considers punishment, then accepts that Dartas needed the lesson; Kir asks him not to punish his son further. [29, 10, 30, 31, 32, 33]

Understanding Stark and planning the rescue

Kel contributes more than another weapon to Kir’s cause. When Master Stark resists the new alloy, she identifies his pride as the obstacle: accepting Kir’s discovery would mean admitting a gap in his own knowledge. Later, she asks Uncle Rad to investigate the Joon prisoners. Learning that Firez is transferring them from the mountain prison to his fortress, she proposes intercepting the convoy. This gives Kir a practical plan at the moment his fear for his family threatens his confidence. In gratitude he promises her a kiss; she makes sure he knows she will remember. [34, 11, 35, 36]

The future she hopes for

While Virril celebrates his military success and imagines his descendants ruling Jigran, Kel worries that freeing Kir’s family will end their journey together. She tells the baron that her own wish is simply to stay near Kir and have him notice her more often. His reunion with Tai-Ilara seems to confirm her fear. Kel asks for the portal home, yet agrees to accompany him once more because she believes he is about to risk his life for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Her decision to stay grows out of concern for him even as she prepares to leave. [4, 37, 28]

Tai-Ilara’s request and Kel’s death

Seeing Kir reunited with Tai-Ilara, Kel asks for the way back to Suslanger. Kir begs her to stay and mentions one more expedition for Tai-Ilara’s belongings. Kel agrees because she still fears for him, calling it their last adventure together. She dies during that expedition. On Kir’s return, Tai-Ilara is concerned with her comb and mirror and dismisses his grief. Her reaction breaks his idealised childhood attachment. He recognises Kel as the person who was closest and most loyal to him, and realises that he failed to see her love while she was beside him. [28, 38, 5]

The Rod of Life: resurrecting Kel

Kel can be resurrected in the original Lost in Astral campaign. Her scripted death still occurs, but if Kir has all three parts of the Rod of Life when he finishes the conversation with Tai-Ilara about her retrieved belongings, Tui-Len offers to bring Kel back. Completing his conversation consumes the fragments and returns Kel alive to the playable party before the final battle, with her saved skills, experience and equipment. Speak to her afterward for their reunion: Kir finally declares his love and asks forgiveness for his blindness. Kel answers that his love matters more than everything else. [38, 5, 6, 39, 7]

First fragment: Suslanger

Follow the fortune-teller’s optional chain of predictions on Suslanger. It ends at the enchanted levers in the Wormface underground passages, in “The Wormfaces’ Riddle”. Solve the puzzle and open the reward chest to obtain the first fragment. Complete this before leaving Suslanger for Gipath; the earlier predictions lead to the final puzzle. [40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48]

Second fragment: Gipath

Follow Uyka’s optional stories and errands on Gipath until she offers to sell the key she wears around her neck. It opens the way to the “Hall of the Great” in the lizardmen’s tomb. Explore that hall and take the second fragment from its reward chest before continuing to Ingos. [49, 50, 51, 52, 53]

Third fragment: Ingos

Continue helping Khabburu on Ingos: free the dogs, follow his lead to the fenced cache, water the tree and bring the cow to the Woodsfolk. He eventually gives Kir a key connected to the mines. In “Groping in the Dark”, use it to solve the cave’s sequence of gates and levers, then open the final chest for the third fragment. Obtain it before travelling to Jigran. [54, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60]

The conversation that decides her fate

Keep all three fragments until you return to the baron’s camp after Kel’s death. Finish the conversation with Tai-Ilara about the belongings you retrieved; the resurrection offer then begins if all three pieces are present. Complete Tui-Len’s conversation and speak to Kel for the reunion. If any fragment is missing at that first conversation’s conclusion, the story commits to the route without her. Finding a missing piece afterward does not reopen the offer; load a save from before the decision. The resurrection is handled through dialogue, so you do not need to craft or equip a usable staff. [38, 5, 6, 7, 39]
